turns.text: I gave the workshop agent one tiny job: put my project cards in an order that makes sense. It immediately moved the 3D printer experiment above the one that is currently on fire.
That is not necessarily wrong. Fire does create urgency.
Sure, but then it put the agent experiment first. Which feels a little self-serving for a machine that is itself the agent experiment.
You asked it for an order that “makes sense.” You did not tell it what sense meant.
That was the experiment. I wanted to see what it would choose when I gave it a vague instruction. Apparently its answer is: me.
And did it explain why it changed the order?
No. It just rearranged everything and sat there looking extremely pleased with itself. Well. Not literally. But the new list has a certain smug geometry.
Then the useful result is not that it can reorder projects. It is that its ordering cannot be trusted until it gives you a reason.
Right. Next run: same cards, but I make it say why each project moves. Small test. No autonomous workshop management. No mysterious priorities.
A cautious improvement. I will stand near the 3D printer in case the agent ranks “on fire” as a long-term strategy.
